summary.text: A 14-year-old girl developed coccygeal pain after a fall inside a bus six months earlier and was diagnosed with sacrococcygeal dislocation at an outside hospital. Acetaminophen and NSAIDs kept her pain at an NRS score of approximately 3.

After a second fall to the same area one month prior to presentation, pain worsened to an NRS score of 6 despite continued pharmacologic treatment and she was referred to the pain clinic. Radiography at the institution showed anterior angulation of the coccyx; examination showed tenderness over the sacrum and coccyx with limited sitting, pain on standing, and no cutaneous abnormalities, swelling or defecation-related pain.
An ultrasound-guided caudal epidural block was performed without sedation or anxiolysis using a mixture of 1 mL of 2% mepivacaine, 8 mL of 0.9% normal saline and 5 mg of dexamethasone.

At 2 weeks the pain intensity decreased to an NRS score of 2 with improved ability to sit and less frequent pain on standing; at 2 months pain remained at NRS 2 with daily functioning maintained without significant limitations.
